symptom: a change in bowel habit put down to a new diet
hook: An apple eaten down to the core in the middle of a smooth hose.
whatYouSee: A short ragged apple core narrowing with overhanging shoulders in the colon on the left side of the patient.
whyItMatters: Carcinoma of the large bowel can encircle the lumen and produce an apple core narrowing that leads to large bowel obstruction. Suspected tumours need histology and a staging CT.
treatment: If biopsy confirms cancer the usual treatment is surgical resection of the involved segment after staging. Obstructing tumours may first need decompression by a stent or colostomy.
takeaway: An apple core stricture with overhanging edges on barium enema is colon cancer until proven otherwise.

observations.observed: AP double-contrast barium enema is confirmed. On the patient's left side (image right), in the descending colon transitioning to sigmoid, there is a focal segment of abrupt circumferential narrowing approximately 3-5 cm in length with a nodular irregular ragged lumen and sharply overhanging shelf-like shoulders at both ends producing a classic apple-core configuration. Colon above and below this stricture is well-distended with barium coating and air with normal haustral folds. The right colon including ascending colon and hepatic flexure appears normal with preserved haustration. Lumbar vertebrae and pelvic bones appear skeletally mature and normal without osseous lesion. Sigmoid/rectosigmoid is relatively under-distended but this does not obscure the primary lesion.

observations.expected: The visible anatomy matches the requested double-contrast barium enema AP and the declared age and anatomical exceptions.
observations.observed: The projection is AP double-contrast barium enema. The skeleton shows skeletally mature adult pelvis and lumbar spine consistent with an adult over 60. No anatomical impossibilities are identified. The under-distension of the distal sigmoid and mild bowel overlap at the hepatic flexure are within expected acquisition variability for this examination.

findings: Anteroposterior projection of the abdomen demonstrating a double-contrast barium enema study
The entire large bowel is opacified with barium coating the mucosal surface and air providing luminal distension, outlining the colon from rectum to cecum
Normal haustral folds are visible throughout most of the colon
In the mid-descending colon on the left side there is a focal area of mucosal irregularity with a nodular, lobulated filling defect and altered fold pattern, producing an irregular luminal narrowing
The remainder of the colon demonstrates relatively preserved haustral pattern without diffuse mucosal granularity
No evidence of free intraperitoneal air is seen
Lumbar spine and pelvis are visible; no osseous lesions are apparent on this view
Rectal catheter tip is not clearly visible, suggesting retrograde filling technique
differential: Colorectal adenocarcinoma: the focal irregular mucosal mass with luminal narrowing in the descending colon is most consistent with a primary colonic carcinoma
Annular or polypoid adenoma with malignant transformation: a large polyp or villous adenoma could produce this degree of lobulated mucosal irregularity
Diverticular disease with associated mucosal distortion: less likely given the focal lobulated character, but segmental spasm or pericolic inflammation from diverticulitis can mimic a mass lesion
anatomyConcerns: The sigmoid colon and rectosigmoid junction appear relatively under-distended compared to more proximal segments, which could mask additional lesions in this region
The hepatic flexure region shows somewhat redundant bowel loop overlap, limiting full mucosal assessment in that area
No small bowel opacification is present, consistent with a large-bowel-only study

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The independent reading identifies a focal area of nodular, lobulated mucosal irregularity with luminal narrowing in the mid-descending/sigmoid colon on the patient's left (image right). The double-contrast barium enema shows abrupt circumferential narrowing with overhanging shelf-like shoulders at both ends and an irregular ragged lumen through the stricture segment — the classic apple-core morphology. This short, abrupt, shouldered circumferential stricture with destroyed mucosal pattern is the hallmark discriminator for annular colorectal carcinoma rather than a polyp/adenoma (which would be polypoid/pedunculated without complete circumferential shouldering) or diverticular disease (which shows spasm/sacculation without true mucosal destruction). The remainder of the colon shows preserved haustration bilaterally. The sigmoid/rectosigmoid is under-distended but the primary lesion is clearly visible. Hepatic flexure overlap is a normal projection effect from redundant bowel. No unexplained additional lesion is identified.
